Dry eye is one of the most common ocular surface problems today, affecting 32% of Indians (AIOS data, 2023). When the tear film becomes unstable, the cornea—the clear front window of the eye—starts to dry out, leading to burning, redness, fluctuating vision, and light sensitivity. Dr Kavita Rao, leading cornea specialist in Bandra–Khar, explains that untreated dry eye can gradually cause corneal surface damage, tiny epithelial defects, and increased risk of infections.

Screen overuse, air‑conditioned environments, ageing, hormonal changes, and certain medications worsen symptoms. Many patients assume it is “normal tiredness,” but persistent dryness needs evaluation. Treatment ranges from lubricating drops and warm compresses to advanced options like punctal plugs or serum drops, depending on severity.

Protecting the cornea early prevents long‑term complications. If you experience gritty sensation, blurred vision that improves after blinking, or discomfort by evening, get your eyes examined promptly.

After cataract surgery, proper post-operative care is essential for a successful result. Dr Kavita Rao, an ophthalmologist in Khar West, Bandra, says that patients typically experience improved vision within a few days, but full recovery takes around four to six weeks.

Immediately after surgery, your eye doctor will provide protective eyewear and prescribe medicated eye drops to prevent infection and reduce inflammation. Avoid rubbing your eyes, strenuous activities, and exposure to dust and water for at least a week. 

Wearing sunglasses outdoors helps protect your eyes from bright light and UV rays. Common side effects include mild irritation, redness, and sensitivity to light, but these usually subside quickly. 

Visit your eye doctor for all follow-up appointments to monitor healing progress. If you experience severe pain, vision loss, or persistent redness, contact your eye surgeon immediately. According to the American Academy of Ophthalmology, over 95% of cataract surgeries are successful in restoring vision, making post-operative care crucial for optimal results.

Cataracts are a major eye problem. Dr Kavita Rao, eye surgeon at PD Hinduja Hospital, Khar West, shares some insights on this issue.
While we can't completely prevent cataracts, there are ways to lower your risk. Wearing sunglasses to protect your eyes from UV rays, eating a healthy diet full of antioxidants, and avoiding smoking are all great steps to take. Regular eye check-ups are also super important for catching any issues early.

In India, cataracts are the leading cause of blindness, making up 66.2% of blindness cases in people over 50. The National Blindness and Visual Impairment Survey (2015-2019) found that 93% of blindness cases and 96.2% of visual impairment cases in this age group were avoidable. This really shows how crucial it is to get timely eye care.

Dr Kavita Rao emphasises that while we might not be able to stop cataracts completely, taking care of our eyes can delay their onset and progression.
For an eye checkup, visit our eye clinic in Bandra, Khar West.

Corneal transplant surgery is surrounded by myths that often worry patients unnecessarily.
Dr Kavita Rao, ophthalmologist in Bandra, Mumbai clarifies that modern corneal transplants are among the most successful organ transplants worldwide (EBI).

Myth vs Fact:
· Myth: Recovery takes months
Fact: Most patients resume routine activities in weeks
· Myth: Rejection is very common
Fact: Rejection rates are low with proper care
· Myth: It’s risky
Fact: It’s a safe, wellestablished procedure
With timely surgery and followup, outcomes are excellent.

When keratoconus progresses and glasses or lenses no longer help, a corneal transplant can restore clear vision. India performs over 40,000 corneal transplants annually (Eye Bank Association of India), with high success rates due to modern surgical techniques.

Dr Kavita Rao, experienced in corneal surgeries at P. D. Hinduja Hospital, explains that transplants are recommended when scarring or thinning severely affects vision.

Benefits of corneal transplant:
· Improved clarity
· Reduced distortion
· Longterm stability
· High success rates with proper followup
Early evaluation helps determine the right time for surgery.

Healthy corneas depend on small, consistent habits. In India’s dusty, sunny climate, these habits matter even more.
Dr Kavita Rao explains that the cornea stays healthy when it’s protected from dryness, UV rays, and infections.

Daily habits that help:
· Avoid rubbing your eyes
· Keep contact lenses clean and replace them on time
· Wear UVprotected sunglasses
· Stay hydrated
· Follow the 202020 rule for screen use
· Maintain clean hands and makeup hygiene

These simple steps reduce the risk of infections, abrasions, and longterm corneal damage.

A mild red eye after long screen hours may be harmless. But a red eye with severe pain, sudden vision drop, white spots on the cornea, or intense light sensitivity can indicate a corneal emergency.

Corneal ulcers are especially common in India due to dust, trauma, and improper contact lens hygiene (AIOS).
Dr Kavita Rao stresses that corneal ulcers can progress within hours, making early treatment essential.

Seek urgent care if you notice:
· Severe redness
· Sharp pain
· Blurred vision
· Discharge
· A white/grey spot on the cornea
Prompt treatment prevents scarring and vision loss.

Cataract surgery is a minimally invasive procedure, and most patients have a quick recovery. Dr Kavita Rao, ophthalmologist in Khar, informs that some patients notice improvement in their vision within 24-48 hours, but complete healing typically takes four to six weeks.

During the initial days, mild discomfort, redness, and blurred vision are common, but these gradually subside. Patients are usually advised to avoid strenuous activities, heavy lifting, and rubbing their eyes for at least a week. Driving should be resumed only after confirming with your eye surgeon.
Most people can return to light activities within a few days, but full recovery varies depending on individual health conditions.

Following post-operative instructions, using prescribed eye drops, and visiting your eye doctor for follow-ups help ensure a smooth recovery. If any complications such as severe pain, swelling, or vision loss occur, consult your eye surgeon immediately.

Healthy Vision Month is the perfect time to focus on protecting your eyesight through simple, everyday practices. Dr. Kavita Rao, Ophthalmologist at PD Hinduja Hospital, Mumbai, emphasizes that maintaining eye health is not only about treating conditions—it’s about prevention and lifestyle.

Key steps for healthy vision include:
● Following the 20‑20‑20 rule to ease digital eye strain
● Wearing UV‑protective sunglasses outdoors
● Eating a diet rich in leafy greens, fish, and vitamins that support eye health
● Scheduling regular eye exams to detect issues early
● Encouraging children to get routine vision screenings for better learning outcomes

Ignoring eye health can lead to problems like glaucoma, diabetic eye disease, or severe dryness that affect daily life. Preventive care and timely attention help preserve clear vision for years to come.
This Healthy Vision Month, commit to small changes that make a big difference. With expert guidance from Dr. Kavita Rao at PD Hinduja Hospital, Mumbai, you can enjoy strong, healthy eyes at every stage of life.

Red eyes are common, but not all redness is harmless. In India’s hot, dusty climate, corneal infections and allergies are frequent.

Dr Kavita Rao explains that redness linked to corneal disease often comes with pain, blurred vision, discharge, or light sensitivity — signs that the cornea may be inflamed or infected.

Possible corneal causes of redness:
· Keratitis (infection)
· Dry eye disease
· Allergic eye disease
· Corneal abrasion
· Contact lens complications

Selfmedicating with steroid drops can worsen infections. A proper eye exam helps identify the cause and prevent complications.
